title: Constant-target and constant-source tests for relative universal cones
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent transformations, spaces and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the relative universal diagrams and joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and the quasicategory and Kan-mapping-space assertions of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Let $p:D\to B$ be any functor of quasicategories, let $K$ be any small simplicial set, and let $q:K^{\triangleright}\to D$, with $f=q|_K$ and $x=q(*)$. Write $\alpha:f\to\Delta_Kx$ for the coherent cocone obtained by precomposition with $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$, retaining the initial $K$-vertices labelled $0$ and sending the vertices labelled $1$ to the apex. Then $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if for every vertex $z$ of $D$ the following square of spaces is a homotopy pullback:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_D(x,z)&\xrightarrow{u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(f,\Delta_Kz)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_B(px,pz)&\xrightarrow{v\mapsto\Delta_K(v)(p\alpha)}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(pf,\Delta_K(pz)).
\end{array}$$
Composition and commutativity here include their coherent homotopies. For a homotopy-commuting square, the path-pullback comparison sends a point to its two images together with the specified path between their images in the lower-right corner; this comparison must be a weak homotopy equivalence, and all higher simplices of the path data are retained. Equivalently, in the all-diagrams testing square defining a $p$-colimit diagram, it suffices to take the target diagram to be constant at each $z$ on $K^{\triangleright}$. The passage between these two tests is natural in $p$ and in restriction along any simplicial map $L\to K$, including the induced coherent cocones; the apex is unchanged by restriction. Dually, if $q:K^{\triangleleft}\to D$ has apex $x$ and boundary $f$, it is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $D$, the square with upper row
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(z,x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\Delta_Kz,f)$$
and lower row the corresponding square in $B$, induced by its coherent cone, is a homotopy pullback. Equivalently, only constant source test diagrams are needed. All objects lie in fixed sufficiently large universes. No fibration hypothesis on $p$ and no existence of any other limits or colimits is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, equivalence of conditions (2) and (3), and its colimit dual; apex form obtained from the constant-diagram test by restriction to the cone vertex (the cone-vertex inclusion is one-sided anodyne; restriction gives the constant-target mapping-space equivalence). Coherent cocones use 4.6.5.10. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; read online, archival source WANTED.

proof.text:
We prove the limit orientation first, because [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] states its varying-boundary formula for left cones. Write a left cone $q$ as $(x,f,\alpha:\Delta_Kx\to f)$ and an arbitrary source cone $t$ as $(z,g,\beta:\Delta_Kz\to g)$. Put
$$A_D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(g,f),\quad C_D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\Delta_Kz,f),\quad M_D=\operatorname{Map}_D(z,x),$$
and define $A_B,C_B,M_B$ by applying $p$. The join-cone formula gives, naturally with the boundary projection,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},D)}(t,q)\simeq A_D\times^h_{C_D}M_D.$$
Here the two maps are $a\mapsto a\beta$ and $u\mapsto\alpha\Delta_K(u)$; the path is the coherence of a map of cones. The same formula holds in $B$, and its naturality identifies postcomposition by $p$ with the map between these two path pullbacks. This is the varying-boundary formula, rather than the fixed-boundary cone-fiber formula. All six spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, condition (2); mapping-space reformulation; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text:
For $t$ constant at $z$, its boundary is $\Delta_Kz$ and $\beta$ is the identity. Thus $A_D=C_D$ and the first map into $C_D$ is the identity; the constant-path map
$$M_D\longrightarrow C_D\times^h_{C_D}M_D$$
is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], since an identity is a Kan fibration. This equivalence is over $C_D$, with the map $u\mapsto\alpha\Delta_K(u)$, and the same holds naturally in $B$. The invariance theorem [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] therefore identifies the constant-source all-diagrams square with the apex square $M_D\to C_D$ over $M_B\to C_B$. The comparison retains the coherence path and every higher simplex. In particular the all-diagrams condition of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] implies the displayed constant-source criterion, and testing only constant source diagrams is equivalent to testing this apex square.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, (2) implies (3), and apex identification; agent proof using the existing varying-boundary join-cone mapping formula.

proof.text:
Assume the apex square is a homotopy pullback for every $z$, and fix $t=(z,g,\beta)$. Put $P_D=A_D\times^h_{C_D}M_D$ and $P_B=A_B\times^h_{C_B}M_B$, with the maps and coherence of step 1. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] twice, in its transposed form, to the following two diagrams (rows are displayed in order):
$$\begin{array}{ccc}P_D&\longrightarrow&A_D\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ M_D&\longrightarrow&C_D\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ M_B&\longrightarrow&C_B\end{array}\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}P_D&\longrightarrow&A_D\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ P_B&\longrightarrow&A_B\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ M_B&\longrightarrow&C_B.\end{array}$$
In the first diagram the upper square is the defining path pullback and the lower square is the assumed apex square, so the outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback. In the second diagram the lower square is the defining path pullback; its outer rectangle is the one just obtained. Cancellation therefore makes its upper square a homotopy pullback. Transposing pasting is the same ordinary-pullback associativity in the path/fibration models; [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] and [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] identify these models. The specified homotopy of each defining square is its path coordinate, and the outer homotopies concatenate with the coherence of $p$ supplied in step 1; thus the two outer rectangles use the same homotopy. Step 1 identifies the resulting square $P_D\to A_D$ over $P_B\to A_B$ with the all-source test of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Since $t$ is arbitrary, $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram. No map induced by $p$ is assumed to be a fibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.1.11, transitivity and cancellation, applied twice to path-pullback squares, including their specified homotopies; agent mapping-space proof of the implication (3) implies (2) of Proposition 7.1.6.19 (02X1).

proof.text: Apply the natural mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-op-mapping-reversal] to the testing squares for $p$ and $p^{\mathrm{op}}$. That statement exchanges precomposition and postcomposition and compares their specified commutation homotopies, not only their maps on components. The all-Kan zigzag and path-pullback reversal of [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag], followed by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], therefore preserve and reflect the homotopy-pullback test. Degreewise reversal exchanges the two ordered join blocks, giving $(K^{\triangleright})^{\mathrm{op}}=(K^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleleft}$; it also identifies the opposite functor simplicial sets, by reversing the parameter simplex. Hence a right cone and a constant target become a left cone and a constant source. Under these identifications, the reversed map $\alpha\Delta(u)$ is $\Delta(u)\alpha$, with its reversed coherence path. The limit result of steps 1--3 for $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is thus exactly the colimit and constant-target criteria of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Reversal twice restores the tests, so both implications follow.

source.place: Opposite dual of Proposition 7.1.6.19; agent application of the existing composition-compatible mapping reversal, all-Kan opposite zigzag, and path-pullback invariance statements.

proof.text: The comparison in step 1 is natural in the indexing simplicial set, the target quasicategory, and both cones by [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. For $L\to K$, precomposition restricts $f,g,\alpha,\beta$, sends a boundary transformation $a$ to $a|_L$, and leaves the apex maps $u$ unchanged. The identity $(a\beta)|_L=(a|_L)(\beta|_L)$, and the corresponding identity for $\alpha\Delta(u)$, identify the horizontal maps and their coherence paths with their restrictions. Postcomposition by $p$ commutes with each of these operations. The path-pullback maps apply these operations to all three entries, including the path; hence the apex identifications and the test comparisons commute naturally with them. The same calculation after the opposite construction gives colimit naturality. This is naturality of the comparisons between tests; it does not assert that a relative colimit or limit remains universal after changing its indexing shape.

lean.note: The apex mapping-space square is represented by the canonical evaluation/restriction spans, whose evaluation legs are asserted weak equivalences.
